quotes.text: The problem is that the music itself is not exciting; it's technical enough and performed well, but there's nothing about these seven songs that absolutely grabs the listener and makes them want to listen more.

these performances are simply musically proficient. They don't inspire the listener or suggest that they are listening to greatness. And it's the overall mediocrity of the performances that sinks this one.

It suggests to me, then, that although the shared vocals of Latimer, Bardens and Ferguson are solid enough, they tend to lull the listener into a sense of comfort—so much so, in fact, that they take away from the music being presented.
Camel seems to be a disc of unfulfilled ambition, with the occasional flares of greatness shining through.
